overview: Rise 5.99's Crasher is a toolbox of server-crash payloads dispatched from a single PreMotionEvent handler across eighteen modes, with the Packets setting (1-100, default 10) scaling the per-tick modes. Two guard rails protect the user: the handler returns while the integrated server is running or the player is on localhost or 127.0.0.1, and it disables itself within five ticks of a world change. The modes split into four families: chat command spammers (Pex and Multiverse flood server commands, Log4J sends a jndi payload and disables), a tab-complete bomb (FAWE), movement floods and absurd-position claims (Chunk, Fly, Invalid Move, NaN, Rotation, AAC5), and NBT book bombs pushed through window clicks, creative actions and plugin messages (Book, Click, Window, BEdit, One Packet, Mare, Block Click, Interact).

sections.p: The handler bails while the integrated server is running or the player is on 127.0.0.1 or localhost, so a self-hosted test world is never attacked; when the player's ticksExisted is below 5 after a world change, the module disables itself and raises a notification instead of firing. The switch runs once per tick, and onUpdateAlwaysInGui hides the Packets setting unless Mare or Interact is selected, so the setting only exists for the two modes that read it.

Chunk loops 32000 C04PacketPlayerPosition packets in a single tick, incrementing x and z while capping y at 255 and claiming onGround true; Fly first walks 200 steps of +9 in y, to 1800, then 10000 steps of +9 in z from that height; Invalid Move sends a C06 with Double.MAX_VALUE on all three axes and Float.MAX_VALUE yaw and pitch; NaN sends Double.NaN positions and Float.NaN look; Rotation sends a C05 look with 9.223372E18F yaw and pitch; AAC5 sends a C04 at x 1.7E301, y -999, onGround true. Each of these either saturates the server's packet processing or feeds values that vanilla position validation does not bound, and all of them travel through PacketUtil.sendPacket.

Book, Click, Window, BEdit and One Packet build writable or written books whose pages carry deeply nested '{extra:[{' chains, up to hundreds of levels of recursion, with random 16-digit author and title fields, and push them as C0E window clicks on slot 0, a C10 creative action, or C17 MC|BEdit payloads; Click and BEdit repeat the construction 30 times in one tick. Mare sends the Packets-setting number of C08 block placements holding a book with an 833-level extra chain at the player's position, and Interact sends the same number of C07 ABORT digs at random positions drawn up to Double.MAX_VALUE; Block Click sends a single C0E carrying a piston-head stack. The recursion chains are the payload: servers that deserialize the nested components without a depth bound exhaust memory or stack.

files.label: Crasher.java
files.explanation: The module file is the whole crash toolbox. onPreMotion runs the guard rails and the eighteen-mode switch, onUpdateAlwaysInGui hides the Packets setting unless Mare or Interact is selected, and each mode constructs its packets inline through PacketUtil. The NBT builders are duplicated per mode rather than factored out, so the recursion-chain payloads are assembled independently in Book, Click, Window, BEdit, One Packet and Mare, with only the container packet and the item differing.

files.label: PacketUtil.java (send paths)
files.explanation: PacketUtil is the send wrapper every mode uses. sendPacket goes through addToSendQueue, the normal queue that preserves order and fires the client's outgoing-packet events, which is how the floods reach the network layer in the exact sequence the mode builds them; sendPacketWithoutEvent routes through addToSendQueueWithoutEvent, bypassing the event bus, which is the path the FAWE tab-complete mode uses. The distinction matters because the 32000-packet and 10200-packet loops would otherwise re-enter any packet hook the client runs.

countering.label: NoCheatPlus MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
NoCheatPlus's player MorePackets check, invoked per move from MovingListener, scores every serverbound move into data.morePacketsFreq, an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets, and accumulates the window against morePacketsEPSMax (default 22 packets per second with 20 ideal) plus a burst path on the newest half-second bucket (default 15 packets, direct-violation 10).

The Chunk mode's 32000 C04 packets and the Fly mode's 10200 C04 packets land in a single tick, so the newest bucket overflows the direct-violation threshold by three orders of magnitude on the first burst and the default actions cancel at vl>2; the sustained per-tick modes (Mare and Interact) exceed the window ceiling the moment they run more than 22 per second. The check is content-blind: it counts position packets regardless of their values, so the absurd coordinates of Invalid Move and NaN score exactly like ordinary moves.

countering.label: Arc v2 MorePackets (per-second packet ceiling)
countering.explanation:
Vrekt's MorePackets check counts the flying and position packet streams per second. PacketListener increments MovingData's flyingPackets and positionPackets counters on every C03-family packet and runs updateAndCheck, and the check flags when either counter exceeds max-packets (config.yml default 30) and kicks when it exceeds max-packets-kick (default 70), broadcasting the kick as 'sending too many packets'.

The Chunk and Fly floods exceed 70 in the first tick and trigger the kick path directly, and a one-tick flood that stayed under the counters' reset boundary would still cancel subsequent moving packets via setCancelMovingPackets. This is a second, independent rate ceiling on the same flood, and it is packet-level, so servers that reject the position claims still count the traffic.

countering.label: NoCheatPlus SurvivalFly (position physics envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly rebuilds the allowed vertical envelope from the world and never trusts the packet's onGround flag, since ground truth comes from the block cache. The Invalid Move mode's C06 with Double.MAX_VALUE on y, the NaN mode's Double.NaN coordinates, and the AAC5 mode's 1.7E301 claim all produce y-distances beyond any numeric envelope, so the violation (yDistanceAboveLimit plus hDistanceAboveLimit times 100) overflows into an immediate flag and set-back on the first packet; the Fly mode's +9-per-packet climb to y 1800 exceeds the jump envelope by hundreds of blocks per move.

The check also runs its rate path in concert with MorePackets, so the flood modes accumulate on both axes. The honest note is that several of these modes are aimed at vanilla servers with no anticheat; on an NCP server the first absurd C03 is the last one the player effectively sends.

countering.label: Hawk InventoryActions (window clicks without an open window)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's InventoryActions punishes window clicks when its ledger says no inventory is open (hasInventoryOpen() == 0), a state it derives from the S2D window-open, C16 inventory command and close packets.

The crasher's C0E modes (Book, Click, Block Click and the C10 Window variant) fire their clicks with no GUI open by construction, so every click is punished and the player is resynced, regardless of what the click payload carries; the module cannot open a container first because its purpose is the flood, not looting. The check is content-blind to the NBT payloads, so it cannot see the recursion bomb itself, but it converts the click flood into immediate punishment, which is the practical defense against the C0E side of the module.
